name: lowpoly-sim
title: Low-poly simulation
summary: A flat-shaded low-poly world rendered live in three.js: a hazy dusk city, a faceted Earth, a particle galaxy, with a big real-number counter climbing as the scale grows.

look.ground: a dusk city street under a pink-violet gradient sky with fog; deep space (#05040a) once the camera leaves Earth

palette.where: top of the city sky gradient
lit windows, 12 % of them; the rest #4f4655 and #625868 on a #8d7c86 facade
planet seas (#4a8fb5 shallow to #23547f deep); land #5b8a4a grass, #c9a66b desert, white ice

look.type: EB Garamond regular for the what-if question (78 px, centred, top third); Inter 700 tracked caps for the counter label and Inter 400 96 px for the counter; Inter 700 46 px captions in a dark rounded box
look.texture: none: flat facets, fog and glow sprites only; no grain, no film look
look.light: dusk: a warm low key light behind the scene, a pink hemisphere fill, soft shadows; in space one hard white sun from the left
look.materials: MeshStandardMaterial with flatShading, roughness 0.95, no textures except canvas window grids; low-detail icospheres for anything round

consistency: everything is code: the person, the city and the planets are built by functions from a seeded random, so every shot of them is identical; one recurring hero figure seen from behind

motion.feel: a simulation that keeps escalating: steady camera, sudden physical hits
moves: per event: object pops 1 + (0.35..1.25)·e^(-9·dt), the figure recoils sin(min(16·dt, π)) and settles, a ground ring spreads in 0.45 s, the camera nudges
milestone: white flash 0.06 s up and 0.45-1.0 s down that hides a cut, a counter jump to 1.25x and back
scale jump: the camera pulls up and out in one ease (street → rooftops → orbit → solar system → galaxy), fog far distance opening with it
break-up: an icosphere split into Voronoi chunks that fly out with spin, distance ∝ k^1.3
shake: sum of two sines per axis, amplitude set per hit and decaying linearly

pace.text: the question holds over the opening; one caption per milestone, 2.5-5 s each; the counter is always on and changes every frame

banned: smooth shading or photo textures on models
photoreal HDRI skies or lens dirt
a static counter or a fake number: the counter must be a function of the simulated time
more than one hot accent colour in a scene
cuts without a flash or a camera move to carry them
source: original, after first-person what-if simulation shorts
